evidence: log loss +0.0171 (95% interval +0.0011 to +0.0306). The model's probabilities are WORSE than the market's closing probabilities (the interval is above zero).

115 picks, ROI -0.6% (95% interval -18.2% to +14.8%), win rate 59.1% against a break-even 58.5%. Random sides at the same margin match or beat this 29% of the time. Line movement toward the pick after it was made: +0.04 probability points on average (zero means no closing-line value).
How many bets before ROI can be trusted

At the observed spread of results, detecting a true 3% ROI takes about 4,945 bets and a 5% ROI about 1,780; a 1% edge takes 44,497. Closing-line value converges much faster, which is why it is the primary measure.
167 picks, ROI -8.7% (-16.7% to +0.5%): insufficient evidence (interval spans 0).
18 picks, ROI -100.0% (-100.0% to -100.0%): too few picks (<30) to say anything.
